extraction.body: To make the world smarter, happier, and richer. Founded in 1993 by brothers Tom and David Gardner, The Motley Fool helps millions of people around the world achieve their financial goals through our investing services and financial advice. Our goal is to help every Canadian achieve financial freedom. Small-cap stocks can be some of the most exciting investments in the market, offering outsized growth potential as young or under-the-radar companies scale their businesses. Many of today’s large-cap success stories began as small-caps, and investors who identify them early can be rewarded handsomely over the long term. While small-caps are not for the faint-of-heart, they could have a place in your investment portfolio, especially if you’re interested in picking growth stocks . In Canada, small-cap companies often operate in niche industries such as clean technology, mining services, software, healthcare innovation, and industrial manufacturing. While these businesses can benefit disproportionately from economic recoveries, new technology adoption, or favorable commodity cycles, they also face higher risks related to liquidity, customer concentration, and execution. As interest rates stabilize and investors look beyond mega-cap names in 2026, small-caps are once again drawing attention as a potential source of differentiated returns. So what exactly qualifies as a small-cap stock, and how can investors separate high-quality growth opportunities from speculative bets? Below, we’ll explore small-cap investing in more detail and highlight some of the top Canadian small-cap stocks to watch in 2026. A small-cap is a type of stock , whose market capitalization falls between $300 million and $2 billion. A step up in size from micro-cap stocks (companies with market caps between $50 – $300 million), small-caps are often small companies with the potential for growth and higher returns, but less profits and stability than older, more established companies. They can be highly volatile, though. Over long periods of time, they tend to outperform mid- and large-caps. Large-cap stocks are companies with market caps higher than $10 billion. These are large companies with well-established brands, such as Royal Bank of Canada, Enbridge, and Canadian National Railway. In general, large-cap stocks are less volatile and more stable than small-cap companies. Their larger market capitalization and higher outstanding shares give large-cap companies more financial muscle and deeper cash reserves, while their competitive position anchors them during deeply uncertain financial times. Large-cap stocks are often more likely to pay out dividends, too. Docebo (pronounced “doh-che-bo”) ( TSX: DCBO ) is a learning management system that helps companies train their employees, partners, and customers. More than 1,600 companies use Docebo for educational purposes, including Starbucks, Thomson Reuters, Uber, and Samsung. Docebo’s learning platform is both secured by the cloud and powered by Artificial Intelligence (AI). Unlike the lesson planning on most eLearning platforms, which require users to watch lessons and take quizzes in a linear, pre-fabricated timeline, Docebo’s AI curates educational materials based entirely on the needs of each user. You’ll still see the same content as another employee, but Docebo might structure it differently to fit your unique learning style and needs. Docebo is currently trading with a market capitalization of about C$875.26 million, and its financial performance shows steady growth underpinned by recurring subscription revenues. Over the trailing twelve months to September 2025, Docebo generated approximately US$236.7 million in revenue, up more than 13% year-over-year, reflecting ongoing demand for its cloud-based learning platform. 5N Plus Inc. has a current market capitalization of about C$1.64 billion. They have delivered robust financial performance so far in 2025, marked by strong revenue growth and expanding profitability. Revenue for the trailing twelve months recently climbed to roughly US$360 million, up about 27% year-over-year, while Q3 2025 results showed a 33% increase in quarterly revenue to US$104.9 million and an 86% rise in adjusted EBITDA driven by demand in renewable energy and space solar power markets. To find truly great small-cap stocks, you have to learn to separate the bad from the good. Here are three ways to start digging for the best small-caps. First, look for companies that have the potential to disrupt entire industries. For instance, you might look for companies that have a solid line of products (or ideas) that no other company in their industry is offering. Or you might look for a company that has a compelling business model or a way of earning revenue that differs from others. Or you might look for companies that are using technology in ways others just aren’t. Take banking, for instance. Many bank stocks are attached to banks that continue to do things the way they always have. But plenty of small fintech companies are challenging this traditional model with touch-free banking services, robo-investing, and even broker-free mortgages. These companies (often small-caps) are worth watching, as they could easily attract scores of people from all generations. But new tech companies aren’t the only industry disruptors. While, yes, in the past decade, many of the most innovative companies have been tech, we’ve seen retailers (lululemon) and consumer discretionary companies ( Tesla ) take a stab at convention. You just have to keep your eyes open for potentially explosive ideas. If the stock is extremely expensive, but the company isn’t making that much money, the stock may be overpriced. Likewise, if the stock is making lots of money, but the stock price is low, you may have found a deal. The main reason to invest in small-caps is the potential for higher returns. Unlike many large-caps, which offer security but limited growth potential, small-caps could grow immensely over long periods of time. Many small-caps end up being the kinds of stocks investors wish they had invested in before they grew into large- or mega-caps. When you hear people say, “I invested in Amazon when it was just starting out,” you’re hearing a story of successful small-cap investing. But, of course, for every small-cap that becomes an Amazon, there are thousands of small-caps that fizzle out. Perhaps the greatest risk with small-caps, then, is the fact that they lack the resources that bigger companies have. Many just aren’t profitable yet, which is okay for the short-term, but devastating for the long run. The reason is fairly simple. During bull markets, a stronger economy gives small-caps more space to capture consumers’ attention. During bull markets, consumers typically have more discretionary income, allowing them to try new products and services. Small-cap investing is a great way to gain immense wealth. But they’re not for everyone. If your risk tolerance is fairly low, or if you’re near retirement, you may want to stick with safer investments, such as large-caps and blue chips. Additionally, because many small-caps are relatively unknown, you might want to stick with companies you understand, especially if you’re not the do-it-yourself type who will spend hours researching new stock picks. That said, small-caps are great for investors who want to earn more than blue chips, large-caps, or index funds typically allow. They’re also ideal for investors who have a long time horizon, that is, for young (or relatively young) investors who have a long way until retirement. Since many small-caps are just getting off the ground, it could take years before they hit their growth potential, with many ups and downs along the way. As long as you take a buy-and-hold strategy, focusing on long-term growth and not short-term price movements, you’ll put yourself in a good place to earn the utmost growth. Keep in mind, however, that investing in small-caps can be risky. You definitely want to do your homework before you buy shares in a small-cap company. While the growth potential on small-caps can be amazing, the losses can be devastating. Use evaluation metrics and analysis to dig into your stock picks, and you’ll avoid investing in a dud. If you’re not the kind of person who enjoys picking stocks , you could buy shares in a small-cap-focused exchange-traded fund (ETF) . Basically, with an ETF, you’ll spread your money across numerous different small-cap stocks. Your ETF manager will pick the stocks for you, and your shares will grow as the cumulative performance of all the small-caps grows. Should you invest $1,000 in Absolute Software right now? Small-cap stocks can be some of the most exciting investments in the market, offering outsized growth potential as young or under-the-radar companies scale their businesses. Many of today’s large-cap success stories began as small-caps, and investors who identify them early can be rewarded handsomely over the long term. While small-caps are not for the faint-of-heart, they could have a place in your investment portfolio, especially if you’re interested in picking growth stocks .

In Canada, small-cap companies often operate in niche industries such as clean technology, mining services, software, healthcare innovation, and industrial manufacturing. While these businesses can benefit disproportionately from economic recoveries, new technology adoption, or favorable commodity cycles, they also face higher risks related to liquidity, customer concentration, and execution. As interest rates stabilize and investors look beyond mega-cap names in 2026, small-caps are once again drawing attention as a potential source of differentiated returns.

So what exactly qualifies as a small-cap stock, and how can investors separate high-quality growth opportunities from speculative bets? Below, we’ll explore small-cap investing in more detail and highlight some of the top Canadian small-cap stocks to watch in 2026.

A small-cap is a type of stock , whose market capitalization falls between $300 million and $2 billion. A step up in size from micro-cap stocks (companies with market caps between $50 – $300 million), small-caps are often small companies with the potential for growth and higher returns, but less profits and stability than older, more established companies.
They can be highly volatile, though. Over long periods of time, they tend to outperform mid- and large-caps.
Large-cap stocks are companies with market caps higher than $10 billion. These are large companies with well-established brands, such as Royal Bank of Canada, Enbridge, and Canadian National Railway.

In general, large-cap stocks are less volatile and more stable than small-cap companies. Their larger market capitalization and higher outstanding shares give large-cap companies more financial muscle and deeper cash reserves, while their competitive position anchors them during deeply uncertain financial times. Large-cap stocks are often more likely to pay out dividends, too.

Docebo (pronounced “doh-che-bo”) ( TSX: DCBO ) is a learning management system that helps companies train their employees, partners, and customers. More than 1,600 companies use Docebo for educational purposes, including Starbucks, Thomson Reuters, Uber, and Samsung.

Docebo’s learning platform is both secured by the cloud and powered by Artificial Intelligence (AI). Unlike the lesson planning on most eLearning platforms, which require users to watch lessons and take quizzes in a linear, pre-fabricated timeline, Docebo’s AI curates educational materials based entirely on the needs of each user. You’ll still see the same content as another employee, but Docebo might structure it differently to fit your unique learning style and needs.

Docebo is currently trading with a market capitalization of about C$875.26 million, and its financial performance shows steady growth underpinned by recurring subscription revenues. Over the trailing twelve months to September 2025, Docebo generated approximately US$236.7 million in revenue, up more than 13% year-over-year, reflecting ongoing demand for its cloud-based learning platform.

5N Plus Inc. has a current market capitalization of about C$1.64 billion. They have delivered robust financial performance so far in 2025, marked by strong revenue growth and expanding profitability. Revenue for the trailing twelve months recently climbed to roughly US$360 million, up about 27% year-over-year, while Q3 2025 results showed a 33% increase in quarterly revenue to US$104.9 million and an 86% rise in adjusted EBITDA driven by demand in renewable energy and space solar power markets.
To find truly great small-cap stocks, you have to learn to separate the bad from the good. Here are three ways to start digging for the best small-caps.

First, look for companies that have the potential to disrupt entire industries. For instance, you might look for companies that have a solid line of products (or ideas) that no other company in their industry is offering. Or you might look for a company that has a compelling business model or a way of earning revenue that differs from others. Or you might look for companies that are using technology in ways others just aren’t.

Take banking, for instance. Many bank stocks are attached to banks that continue to do things the way they always have. But plenty of small fintech companies are challenging this traditional model with touch-free banking services, robo-investing, and even broker-free mortgages. These companies (often small-caps) are worth watching, as they could easily attract scores of people from all generations.

But new tech companies aren’t the only industry disruptors. While, yes, in the past decade, many of the most innovative companies have been tech, we’ve seen retailers (lululemon) and consumer discretionary companies ( Tesla ) take a stab at convention. You just have to keep your eyes open for potentially explosive ideas.

If the stock is extremely expensive, but the company isn’t making that much money, the stock may be overpriced. Likewise, if the stock is making lots of money, but the stock price is low, you may have found a deal.

The main reason to invest in small-caps is the potential for higher returns. Unlike many large-caps, which offer security but limited growth potential, small-caps could grow immensely over long periods of time. Many small-caps end up being the kinds of stocks investors wish they had invested in before they grew into large- or mega-caps. When you hear people say, “I invested in Amazon when it was just starting out,” you’re hearing a story of successful small-cap investing.

But, of course, for every small-cap that becomes an Amazon, there are thousands of small-caps that fizzle out. Perhaps the greatest risk with small-caps, then, is the fact that they lack the resources that bigger companies have. Many just aren’t profitable yet, which is okay for the short-term, but devastating for the long run.

The reason is fairly simple. During bull markets, a stronger economy gives small-caps more space to capture consumers’ attention. During bull markets, consumers typically have more discretionary income, allowing them to try new products and services.

Small-cap investing is a great way to gain immense wealth. But they’re not for everyone. If your risk tolerance is fairly low, or if you’re near retirement, you may want to stick with safer investments, such as large-caps and blue chips.

Additionally, because many small-caps are relatively unknown, you might want to stick with companies you understand, especially if you’re not the do-it-yourself type who will spend hours researching new stock picks.

That said, small-caps are great for investors who want to earn more than blue chips, large-caps, or index funds typically allow. They’re also ideal for investors who have a long time horizon, that is, for young (or relatively young) investors who have a long way until retirement.

Since many small-caps are just getting off the ground, it could take years before they hit their growth potential, with many ups and downs along the way. As long as you take a buy-and-hold strategy, focusing on long-term growth and not short-term price movements, you’ll put yourself in a good place to earn the utmost growth.

Keep in mind, however, that investing in small-caps can be risky. You definitely want to do your homework before you buy shares in a small-cap company. While the growth potential on small-caps can be amazing, the losses can be devastating. Use evaluation metrics and analysis to dig into your stock picks, and you’ll avoid investing in a dud.

If you’re not the kind of person who enjoys picking stocks , you could buy shares in a small-cap-focused exchange-traded fund (ETF) . Basically, with an ETF, you’ll spread your money across numerous different small-cap stocks. Your ETF manager will pick the stocks for you, and your shares will grow as the cumulative performance of all the small-caps grows.

Since then, many stocks in the semiconductor, cloud computing, and even software industries have delivered blistering returns, leading the broader market higher. But volatility is on the rise as investors question the sustainability of the AI infrastructure spending boom. Practically every stock in the AI sphere is pulling back, including some of the highest-quality names: Corrections are a normal part of the investing journey, but investors who want to limit their exposure to extreme volatility might want to consider buying an exchange-traded fund (ETF) like the iShares Future AI and Tech ETF ( ARTY -4.63% ) . It holds a portfolio of 50 leading AI stocks, so it saves investors from having to pick winners and losers. Read on. The iShares Future AI and Tech ETF aims to give investors exposure to the entire AI value chain, which includes infrastructure, software, and services. Below are a couple of its most noteworthy holdings from each of those categories. Some of the other noteworthy AI stocks in the iShares ETF include Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing , Broadcom , Micron Technology , and Space Exploration Technologies . The iShares Future AI and Tech ETF was originally created in 2018 with a focus on AI and robotics, but it was restructured in August 2024 to narrow its mandate to AI alone. As a result, it doesn't have a very long track record of performance for investors to analyze. However, investors should never park all of their money into an ETF that only focuses on one area of the stock market. Concerns are mounting about the sustainability of the AI spending boom as funding gets harder to come by , particularly at favorable terms. Even the best companies are feeling the effects, with Anthropic now expected to go public at a valuation of $1.5 trillion, down from initial expectations of $2 trillion. If these challenges persist, the iShares ETF could suffer a sharp correction. Cost is another consideration. The iShares ETF has an expense ratio of 0.47%, which translates to an annual fee of $47 for every $10,000 invested. That doesn't sound like much at face value, but it's roughly 15 times more than an investor would pay in a passive index fund offered by Vanguard , for example, which can cost as little as 0.03% per year. The iShares ETF's higher fees relate to its actively managed portfolio. Rather than simply tracking an index, a team of professionals will regularly buy and sell stocks based on what they believe will deliver the best returns. This can yield great results, but it also costs more money. In summary, the iShares Future AI and Tech ETF might be the perfect addition to a diversified portfolio that doesn't already have much exposure to the AI industry, but it definitely shouldn't be an investor's only position. extraction.body: Uber and OpenAI announced an expansion of their partnership on Thursday, with the ride-share giant telling TechCrunch that its entire global workforce — some 30,000 people — will now be using ChatGPT Work. ChatGPT Work was introduced in July as an enterprise-focused AI agent that corporate teams could deploy for various workflows. Uber originally piloted ChatGPT Work with 1,000 employees earlier this year but has now scaled up its usage to the entire company. That earlier pilot was deployed to workers from across Uber’s various departments, including finance, operations, and product. Indeed, a majority of the early adopters — some 80% — were non-engineers, Sumanth Sukumar, Uber’s VP of engineering, told TechCrunch. “They used it for a wide range of tasks: analyzing complex data from our operations to identify trends and develop recommendations; localizing training materials for different markets and languages; and building personalized interactive dashboards to manage their daily work,” he said. Yet while the ride-share giant is now going all-in on ChatGPT, it sounds not to have settled on exactly how employees will use it. “Our approach is to make powerful AI tools available across Uber while giving teams room to experiment,” Sukumar said. “For example, earlier this year we paired 30 AI engineers with teams across Uber and gave them two weeks to automate key parts of their job. Those ‘AI pods’ showed us how much opportunity there is when you combine technical expertise with a deep understanding of a particular job.” Uber didn’t disclose how much it’s spending on the new rollout of the chatbot. Instead, Sukumar said the company will track how employees use the tool. “We’ll look at how employees are using the technology, the kinds of workflows they develop and how it helps them work more effectively. We’ll evaluate those outcomes and use what we learn to guide how we deploy AI across the business,” he said. Uber says OpenAI worked closely with the company on integrating the chatbot. OpenAI has moved quickly to scale up its enterprise business as it competes with its chief competitor, Anthropic. Once know largely as a consumer brand, the ChatGPT creator has swiftly gained a loyal following with business customers, while other AI companies have struggled to keep up. extraction.body: Uber just made one of the boldest enterprise AI moves of 2026, deploying OpenAI's ChatGPT Work across its entire 30,000-person workforce. The ride-hailing giant is moving past its earlier pilot phase to give every employee access to the enterprise AI agent, signaling a major bet that generative AI can reshape how one of tech's biggest platforms operates. The company-wide rollout puts Uber at the forefront of large-scale enterprise AI adoption, just as competitors scramble to figure out their own AI strategies. The company confirmed it's rolling out ChatGPT Work to its entire 30,000-employee workforce, expanding far beyond the limited pilot program it previously ran. The deployment represents one of the most aggressive enterprise AI adoptions announced this year, and it arrives at a moment when OpenAI's technology is both ascendant and under fire. The ride-hailing giant isn't sharing many details about how employees will use the AI agent or what specific workflows it's targeting. But the sheer scale of the rollout speaks volumes about Uber's confidence in the technology. At 30,000 seats, this ranks among the largest known ChatGPT Work deployments, putting Uber in rarified company among early enterprise AI adopters. Uber's announcement comes just days after independent safety auditors exposed critical flaws in OpenAI's monitoring systems, raising questions about whether the company can adequately oversee its own models. Those revelations haven't slowed enterprise adoption, but they've certainly complicated the narrative around AI safety. For OpenAI, Uber's deployment is a massive validation of its enterprise strategy. The company has been pushing hard into corporate accounts, positioning ChatGPT Work as the productivity tool that can finally deliver on AI's promise to transform white-collar work. Landing a customer the size of Uber - with operations spanning dozens of countries and complex logistics, customer service, and engineering challenges - proves the technology can handle real-world enterprise complexity. But Uber isn't the only one making big AI bets. Anthropic recently launched Claude Duet, an autonomous agent aimed squarely at professionals, with features like morning briefs and task automation. The competitive pressure is intense, and enterprise customers are suddenly spoiled for choice when it comes to AI agents. When Replit quietly dumped Anthropic for OpenAI, the developer platform's CEO cited cost pressures as a key factor. Enterprise AI pricing is still being figured out, and companies like Uber have enormous leverage to negotiate favorable terms. At 30,000 seats, Uber is almost certainly paying a fraction of list price. Uber's move also highlights how quickly the enterprise AI landscape is consolidating around a few key players. While OpenAI racks up major deployments, the company is dealing with internal turbulence. And just last week, the FBI arrested a Saudi OpenAI employee over a recording device, raising fresh security concerns at a company already under intense scrutiny. The broader question is whether AI agents like ChatGPT Work can actually deliver the productivity gains companies are betting on. Uber operates in a notoriously complex environment, juggling driver relationships, rider experiences, regulatory battles, and rapid international expansion. If ChatGPT Work can prove its value across that kind of operational diversity, it'll be a powerful proof point for enterprise AI. There's also the question of what Uber employees will actually do with the tool. The company isn't saying, but the use cases matter enormously. Enterprise AI is only as good as the workflows it enhances, and poorly implemented AI tools can create more problems than they solve. For now, Uber is betting big that OpenAI's technology is ready for prime time at massive scale. The company's willingness to deploy across its entire workforce suggests it saw compelling results from its pilot program. But the real test comes next, as 30,000 employees start using the tool in their daily work and Uber measures whether AI agents can actually move the needle on productivity. Uber's company-wide ChatGPT Work deployment is a watershed moment for enterprise AI, proving that major corporations are willing to bet on the technology despite ongoing safety concerns and competitive uncertainty. extraction.body: Uber and OpenAI announced an expansion of their partnership on Thursday, with the ride-share giant telling TechCrunch that its entire global workforce — some 30,000 people — will now be using ChatGPT Work. ChatGPT Work was introduced in July as an enterprise-focused AI agent that corporate teams could deploy for various workflows. Uber originally piloted ChatGPT Work with 1,000 employees earlier this year but has now scaled up its usage to the entire company. That earlier pilot was deployed to workers from across Uber’s various departments, including finance, operations, and product. Indeed, a majority of the early adopters — some 80% — were non-engineers, Sumanth Sukumar, Uber’s VP of engineering, told TechCrunch. “They used it for a wide range of tasks: analyzing complex data from our operations to identify trends and develop recommendations; localizing training materials for different markets and languages; and building personalized interactive dashboards to manage their daily work,” he said. Yet while the ride-share giant is now going all-in on ChatGPT, it sounds not to have settled on exactly how employees will use it. “Our approach is to make powerful AI tools available across Uber while giving teams room to experiment,” Sukumar said. “For example, earlier this year we paired 30 AI engineers with teams across Uber and gave them two weeks to automate key parts of their job. Those ‘AI pods’ showed us how much opportunity there is when you combine technical expertise with a deep understanding of a particular job.” Uber didn’t disclose how much it’s spending on the new rollout of the chatbot. Instead, Sukumar said the company will track how employees use the tool. “We’ll look at how employees are using the technology, the kinds of workflows they develop and how it helps them work more effectively. We’ll evaluate those outcomes and use what we learn to guide how we deploy AI across the business,” he said. Uber says OpenAI worked closely with the company on integrating the chatbot. OpenAI has moved quickly to scale up its enterprise business as it competes with its chief competitor, Anthropic. Once know largely as a consumer brand, the ChatGPT creator has swiftly gained a loyal following with business customers, while other AI companies have struggled to keep up. sources.title: ETH news: Ethereum’s four-minute settlement plan could lower the cost of moving crypto - CoinDesk
passages: Ethereum researchers want to cut the wait for a transaction to become final from about 16 minutes to roughly four, a change that could make it cheaper to move money between blockchains.
Ethereum Foundation research counts that idle money as a real cost for these firms, and a shorter wait lets them reuse it sooner.
At four minutes, however, that drops to roughly $67,000.
The 16-minute wait comes down to how Ethereum’s validators vote.
Each one casts a single vote that does two jobs at once, helping pick the next block and helping lock older blocks in for good.
Validators take turns casting those votes, and a block only becomes final after two full rounds of everyone voting.
The draft leaves voting timings, penalties and parts of its security analysis unresolved as of Thursday.
Edgington wrote that “many aspects remain TBD” and that the immediate aim was getting a proposal number — which puts the idea into Ethereum’s formal upgrade pipeline.
Ben Edgington, who coordinates Ethereum’s fast-finality research, filed the draft Wednesday with fellow researchers Francesco D’Amato, Roberto Saltini, Yann Vonlanthen and Mikhail Kalinin.

In the current mechanism, a transaction can land in an Ethereum block well before the network treats it as final, the point where validators, the computers that secure the network, commit to never rewriting it.
Anyone moving funds off Ethereum has to decide when it’s safe to release money on the other side.
Stablecoin providers such as Circle CRCL $87.21 , which issues the dollar-pegged USDC, already charges for speed.
Its fast route from Ethereum currently costs 0.01%, or $1 per $10,000, before network and application charges.
Its standard route carries no Circle transfer fee.
A transfer service can pay them right away from money it already holds there, then wait to get repaid once the original transaction settles.
The customer gets their funds in seconds, and the service has $10,000 tied up until Ethereum is done.
The researchers say splitting the votes would also make it easier to eventually swap in quantum-resistant signatures.
Ethereum would need that upgrade if quantum computers ever get strong enough to break today’s cryptography.
However, four minutes would still be slow next to Solana, which switched on its Alpenglow upgrade Wednesday with a target of finality in about 150 milliseconds.

passages: As a result, Florida voters have returned every judge who has ever faced a retention vote to the bench, regardless of whether they were a Democrat or Republican and whether they were model jurists or connected to scandal.
But the editorial boards of both the Orlando Sentinel and South Florida Sun Sentinel have continued to watch this supreme court for the past six years.

And they both concluded change is needed with the Sentinel’s editorial board saying: “No Supreme Court has ever shown such disrespect for Floridians, or done such damage to basic human rights, consumer protections and fundamental safeguards against corruption and political manipulation.”
Most voters either don’t want — or don’t feel qualified — to do so.
Fortunately, newspapers still take this part of democracy seriously.
After those results went public, embarrassing Muñiz and a few other judges, the Florida Bar stopped conducting surveys and publishing the results … leaving Florida voters with even fewer resources.
By comparison, the ed board recommended keeping all three Rick Scott-appointed judges up for retention in the Fifth District Court of Appeal.
But as long as the state is asking me whether I want Muñiz to keep his post, I’ve seen and read more than enough to know I don’t.
All judges received relatively high scores, ranging from 71% support for retention to 90%, suggesting the majority of attorneys thought they should all stay in office.
Muñiz, you see, used to work for Pam Bondi when she was Florida’s attorney general.
And whenever another scandal popped up — and boy, did they with Bondi — Muñiz, her chief of staff and deputy A.G. at the time, seemed to be in the thick of it.
It can be tough to judge judges — especially since some of the groups that used to help voters assess judicial job performances have stopped doing so. (More on that in a moment.)
In fact, I wrote columns for this newspaper for nearly two decades without ever recommending voters remove a judge from office.
Does this sound like the kind of guy you want making decisions about whether insurance companies, mortgage companies or predatory scammers can run roughshod over consumers?

extraction.body: Every election cycle, Floridians are asked to vote on whether they believe judges on the state’s highest courts deserve to stay on the bench. Yet many Floridians are clueless about how to cast an informed vote. Many don’t even try. In fact, more than a million Floridians who fill out ballots usually leave these “merit retention” questions blank. That’s understandable. It can be tough to judge judges — especially since some of the groups that used to help voters assess judicial job performances have stopped doing so. (More on that in a moment.) Fortunately, newspapers still take this part of democracy seriously. And the Orlando Sentinel’s editorial board has issued a thoughtful split decision this year. Now, I’m not part of the editorial board. Heck, I don’t even always agree with those folks. But I do take their guidance seriously, especially on judges. And this year, the ed board has concluded that three judges deserve to stay, and one needs to go. All were appointed by Republican governors. The only one the ed board wants to boot is Supreme Court Justice Carlos Muñiz. I agree. And that’s not something I say lightly. In fact, I wrote columns for this newspaper for nearly two decades without ever recommending voters remove a judge from office. Muñiz was the first. That was in 2020, during Muñiz’s first merit-retention vote after Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed him. And my reasons were simple: He had a disturbing, anti-consumer record, and his own peers in the legal profession gave him the lowest marks. Muñiz, you see, used to work for Pam Bondi when she was Florida’s attorney general. And whenever another scandal popped up — and boy, did they with Bondi — Muñiz, her chief of staff and deputy A.G. at the time, seemed to be in the thick of it. Why I’m voting ‘No’ on Florida Supreme Court Justice Carlos Muñiz | Commentary For starters, Muñiz was involved in one of Bondi’s earliest scandals when her office ousted the state’s two top mortgage fraud investigators. These were two pit bull attorneys who’d stood up to companies wrongly trying to kick Floridians out of their homes. But then the mortgage companies complained (yes, about the people investigating them), and records showed Muñiz helped justify their oustings. Then there was Bondi’s most infamous scandal when she took $25,000 in campaign cash from Donald Trump and decided not to pursue complaints from Floridians who said they’d been scammed by Donald Trump’s alleged money-making venture, “Trump University.” Muñiz helped defend the office’s inaction — even though New York’s attorney general acted on similar complaints in that state and netted a $25 million settlement for victims there. Does this sound like the kind of guy you want making decisions about whether insurance companies, mortgage companies or predatory scammers can run roughshod over consumers? Also, Muñiz’s own peers in the legal profession gave him the lowest score of any judge in the 2020 merit-retention survey conducted by the Florida Bar. All judges received relatively high scores, ranging from 71% support for retention to 90%, suggesting the majority of attorneys thought they should all stay in office. But Muñiz was at the bottom at 71%. After those results went public, embarrassing Muñiz and a few other judges, the Florida Bar stopped conducting surveys and publishing the results … leaving Florida voters with even fewer resources. But the editorial boards of both the Orlando Sentinel and South Florida Sun Sentinel have continued to watch this supreme court for the past six years. And they both concluded change is needed with the Sentinel’s editorial board saying: “No Supreme Court has ever shown such disrespect for Floridians, or done such damage to basic human rights, consumer protections and fundamental safeguards against corruption and political manipulation.” Endorsement: Support justice by retiring this Supreme Court judge There was a lot more you can read in the piece: “ Support justice by retiring this Supreme Court judge .” By comparison, the ed board recommended keeping all three Rick Scott-appointed judges up for retention in the Fifth District Court of Appeal. The board said John M. Harris, Scott Makar and F. Rand Wallis all deserved to keep their posts in the district that covers 13 counties, including Lake, Seminole, Brevard and Volusia. Endorsement: Retain trio of appeal-court judges Obviously not everyone agrees on Muñiz. As soon as the editorial board issued its recommendation, a number of attorneys rushed to Muñiz’s defense. A trio of recent Florida Bar presidents said they found him to be “intellectually honest and reasonable.” Another local attorney described him in a letter to the editor as “beyond reproach.” I think the record clearly shows otherwise. There’s plenty reproachable about helping oust investigators who were trying to take on fraudulent mortgage companies. And there’s little reasonable about looking the other way when residents say they’re being swindled or when the state’s constitution is being violated. Muniz did show independence when he allowed a citizen amendment on abortion access to get on the state ballot, even though GOP party leaders wanted it off. But such votes have been rare. Also, arguments to deny citizens the chance to vote should’ve never been seriously considered. For the record, I doubt Florida voters will toss any judge out of office on a merit-retention vote this year. Why? Because voters never have. Not once. Most voters either don’t want — or don’t feel qualified — to do so. As a result, Florida voters have returned every judge who has ever faced a retention vote to the bench, regardless of whether they were a Democrat or Republican and whether they were model jurists or connected to scandal. But as long as the state is asking me whether I want Muñiz to keep his post, I’ve seen and read more than enough to know I don’t. Copyright 2026 Orlando Sentinel. All rights reserved. But the editorial boards of both the Orlando Sentinel and South Florida Sun Sentinel have continued to watch this supreme court for the past six years. And they both concluded change is needed with the Sentinel’s editorial board saying: “No Supreme Court has ever shown such disrespect for Floridians, or done such damage to basic human rights, consumer protections and fundamental safeguards against corruption and political manipulation.”

By comparison, the ed board recommended keeping all three Rick Scott-appointed judges up for retention in the Fifth District Court of Appeal. The board said John M. Harris, Scott Makar and F. Rand Wallis all deserved to keep their posts in the district that covers 13 counties, including Lake, Seminole, Brevard and Volusia.
Endorsement: Retain trio of appeal-court judges

Obviously not everyone agrees on Muñiz. As soon as the editorial board issued its recommendation, a number of attorneys rushed to Muñiz’s defense. A trio of recent Florida Bar presidents said they found him to be “intellectually honest and reasonable.” Another local attorney described him in a letter to the editor as “beyond reproach.”
I think the record clearly shows otherwise. There’s plenty reproachable about helping oust investigators who were trying to take on fraudulent mortgage companies.
And there’s little reasonable about looking the other way when residents say they’re being swindled or when the state’s constitution is being violated.

Muniz did show independence when he allowed a citizen amendment on abortion access to get on the state ballot, even though GOP party leaders wanted it off. But such votes have been rare. Also, arguments to deny citizens the chance to vote should’ve never been seriously considered.

For the record, I doubt Florida voters will toss any judge out of office on a merit-retention vote this year. Why? Because voters never have. Not once. Most voters either don’t want — or don’t feel qualified — to do so.

As a result, Florida voters have returned every judge who has ever faced a retention vote to the bench, regardless of whether they were a Democrat or Republican and whether they were model jurists or connected to scandal.
But as long as the state is asking me whether I want Muñiz to keep his post, I’ve seen and read more than enough to know I don’t.

extraction.body: Judges across the country are cautiously exploring the benefits of AI, including one who uses a “brainstorm buddy” to develop questions for oral argument, a National Center for State Courts report shows. The March report is based on surveys of state and federal judges in 10 states and shows that early adopters were using the tech in a variety of ways – but not for “judicial decision making.” “There was unanimous consensus among the judges that, regardless of how they are using GenAI, judges must always remain ‘the deciders’ who determine the ultimate outcome of any legal decision before them,” the report stresses. Researchers granted judges anonymity to encourage participation, and the report also does not name the states. In addition to Chat GPT and Claude, judges listed a handful of models, including Gemini, Grok, HeyGen, Lexis AI Tools, Perplexity, Syno AI, Westlaw/CoCounsel, and “other bespoke court AI tools.” Judges cited efficiency as a primary reason to use AI, and some were excited about the potential to improve access to justice. Several identified projects their court systems are considering, including AI-powered platforms to help self-represented litigants fill out court forms. Every judge was aware of the risk of hallucinations, and some reported requiring their law clerks to sign “acceptable use” agreements. Most judges reported using AI tools for “low risk” administrative chores. “For example, judges discussed using GenAI tools to help plan continuing legal education (CLE) events, to generate ideas or have assistance with drafting speeches, to help plan or update court personnel trainings, and to help create presentation aids, such as slide decks.” Some judges used AI for tasks more associated with traditional judging, including “editorial assistance” with written work, such as summarizing long documents. “For example, some use the technology to create summaries of filings in preparation of oral arguments to help generate questions to ask, or to help generate a list of disputed and undisputed facts,” the report notes. The same judges, however, were careful to stress the importance of verifying the summaries, the report states. At least one judge considered the possibility of using GenAI to help create the first drafts of opinions, “but only when the judge has already independently determined the outcome,” the report states. Most judges who experimented with using AI for legal research reported getting back a hallucinated case, the researchers noted. “As one judge described it, when using GenAI tools to conduct legal research, sometimes you find a needle in a haystack and other times, it’s a swing and a miss.” Judges told researchers they were concerned about how the public would view their use of AI tools, but some also cited the potential to enhance communication with lawyers and the public. One judge suggested using AI to summarize appellate court decisions “at a layperson’s reading level, which the judge could then edit and modify before sharing.” And at least one court system is using AI to revise court rules to “improve their overall readability,” and other judges “are exploring the possibility of using GenAI to facilitate automatic and retroactive sealing and expungement policies,” the report notes. When it comes to future use, some judges said they would appreciate more “practical training in prompt engineering and how best to spot hallucinations and errors,” the report notes. While some judges were excited about increasing access to justices, at least one judge blamed the technology for “dramatic increases” in self-represented litigants and their filings. “The concern is that litigants might have more access to the court, but not access to justice, if such filings overwhelm the system.” ‘To inculcate in its members the principles of duty and service to the public, to improve the administration of justice, and to advance the science of jurisprudence.’ ~ From the Rules Regulating The Florida Bar

extraction.body: Every election cycle, Floridians are asked to vote on whether they believe judges on the state’s highest courts deserve to stay on the bench. Yet many Floridians are clueless about how to cast an informed vote. Many don’t even try. In fact, more than a million Floridians who fill out ballots usually leave these “merit retention” questions blank. That’s understandable. It can be tough to judge judges — especially since some of the groups that used to help voters assess judicial job performances have stopped doing so. (More on that in a moment.) sources.title: Judges explore Artificial Intelligence but keep decision-making human - The Florida Bar
passages: The March report is based on surveys of state and federal judges in 10 states and shows that early adopters were using the tech in a variety of ways – but not for “judicial decision making.”

Judges across the country are cautiously exploring the benefits of AI, including one who uses a “brainstorm buddy” to develop questions for oral argument, a National Center for State Courts report shows.
Judges cited efficiency as a primary reason to use AI, and some were excited about the potential to improve access to justice.
Several identified projects their court systems are considering, including AI-powered platforms to help self-represented litigants fill out court forms.
One judge suggested using AI to summarize appellate court decisions “at a layperson’s reading level, which the judge could then edit and modify before sharing.”

“There was unanimous consensus among the judges that, regardless of how they are using GenAI, judges must always remain ‘the deciders’ who determine the ultimate outcome of any legal decision before them,” the report stresses.

extraction.body: Judges across the country are cautiously exploring the benefits of AI, including one who uses a “brainstorm buddy” to develop questions for oral argument, a National Center for State Courts report shows. The March report is based on surveys of state and federal judges in 10 states and shows that early adopters were using the tech in a variety of ways – but not for “judicial decision making.” “There was unanimous consensus among the judges that, regardless of how they are using GenAI, judges must always remain ‘the deciders’ who determine the ultimate outcome of any legal decision before them,” the report stresses. Researchers granted judges anonymity to encourage participation, and the report also does not name the states. In addition to Chat GPT and Claude, judges listed a handful of models, including Gemini, Grok, HeyGen, Lexis AI Tools, Perplexity, Syno AI, Westlaw/CoCounsel, and “other bespoke court AI tools.” Judges cited efficiency as a primary reason to use AI, and some were excited about the potential to improve access to justice. Several identified projects their court systems are considering, including AI-powered platforms to help self-represented litigants fill out court forms. Every judge was aware of the risk of hallucinations, and some reported requiring their law clerks to sign “acceptable use” agreements. Most judges reported using AI tools for “low risk” administrative chores. “For example, judges discussed using GenAI tools to help plan continuing legal education (CLE) events, to generate ideas or have assistance with drafting speeches, to help plan or update court personnel trainings, and to help create presentation aids, such as slide decks.” Some judges used AI for tasks more associated with traditional judging, including “editorial assistance” with written work, such as summarizing long documents. “For example, some use the technology to create summaries of filings in preparation of oral arguments to help generate questions to ask, or to help generate a list of disputed and undisputed facts,” the report notes. The same judges, however, were careful to stress the importance of verifying the summaries, the report states. At least one judge considered the possibility of using GenAI to help create the first drafts of opinions, “but only when the judge has already independently determined the outcome,” the report states. Most judges who experimented with using AI for legal research reported getting back a hallucinated case, the researchers noted. “As one judge described it, when using GenAI tools to conduct legal research, sometimes you find a needle in a haystack and other times, it’s a swing and a miss.” Judges told researchers they were concerned about how the public would view their use of AI tools, but some also cited the potential to enhance communication with lawyers and the public. One judge suggested using AI to summarize appellate court decisions “at a layperson’s reading level, which the judge could then edit and modify before sharing.” And at least one court system is using AI to revise court rules to “improve their overall readability,” and other judges “are exploring the possibility of using GenAI to facilitate automatic and retroactive sealing and expungement policies,” the report notes. When it comes to future use, some judges said they would appreciate more “practical training in prompt engineering and how best to spot hallucinations and errors,” the report notes. While some judges were excited about increasing access to justices, at least one judge blamed the technology for “dramatic increases” in self-represented litigants and their filings. “The concern is that litigants might have more access to the court, but not access to justice, if such filings overwhelm the system.” ‘To inculcate in its members the principles of duty and service to the public, to improve the administration of justice, and to advance the science of jurisprudence.’ ~ From the Rules Regulating The Florida Bar

sources.title: Dodgers Face Surgery Decision on World Series Hero Will Klein: Report
passages: Dodgers Could Lose Unlikely World Series Hero Klein's injury resonates because of his role in Los Angeles' 2025 championship.
The right-hander became an unexpected hero in Game 3 of the World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays.
Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic reported Thursday that the Dodgers are weighing their next step for Klein.
Klein produced a 1.88 ERA and 7.3% walk rate through May, then recorded a 6.11 ERA with a 15% walk rate beginning in June, according to True Blue LA.
Klein still owns a 3.67 ERA, 49 strikeouts, and two saves across 41 2/3 innings in 36 appearances this season.
The Dodgers initially recalled Wyatt Mills when Klein went on the injured list, but designated Mills for assignment two days later.
Neither Klein nor the Dodgers have said when the discomfort began or whether it contributed to those struggles.
Klein moved into higher-leverage situations and recorded the first two saves of his career.
Klein's absence also eliminates a multi-inning option that could cover emergency starts when needed.

Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic reported Thursday that the Dodgers are weighing their next step for Klein. The likely choices include rest and physical therapy or surgery, according to Ardaya. The new diagnosis makes it unclear whether the 26-year-old will be available for the stretch run or a potential postseason roster. Klein still owns a 3.67 ERA, 49 strikeouts, and two saves across 41 2/3 innings in 36 appearances this season. However, his late command problems and declining results now carry added significance in light of the elbow finding. The Dodgers initially recalled Wyatt Mills when Klein went on the injured list, but designated Mills for assignment two days later. Dodgers Could Lose Unlikely World Series Hero Klein's injury resonates because of his role in Los Angeles' 2025 championship. The right-hander became an unexpected hero in Game 3 of the World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays. Klein had not appeared on the Dodgers' roster during the first three postseason rounds before producing one of the club's defining October performances. Klein moved into higher-leverage situations and recorded the first two saves of his career. Klein's absence also eliminates a multi-inning option that could cover emergency starts when needed. Now the Dodgers must determine whether a conservative approach can calm his elbow or whether removing the bone chips offers the better long-term solution. Until that decision is made, a minimum-length injured-list stay should not be assumed.

sources.title: Will Klein has right elbow surgery to remove bone chips
passages: Dodgers pitcher Will Klein had surgery on Wednesday to remove bone chips and clean up a bone spur in his right elbow, the team announced.
He was placed on the injured list on August 1 with right elbow discomfort and was moved to the 60-day injured list on September 2.

The right-hander pitched five scoreless innings over two games against the Toronto Blue Jays, the highlight a career-best four-inning effort in the marathon Game 3, which needed 18 innings to survive.
Klein was acquired by the Dodgers from the Seattle Mariners in June 2025 and pitched his way onto the World Series roster.

extraction.body: Dodgers pitcher Will Klein had surgery on Wednesday to remove bone chips and clean up a bone spur in his right elbow, the team announced. The right-hander is expected to be ready for spring training. Klein was acquired by the Dodgers from the Seattle Mariners in June 2025 and pitched his way onto the World Series roster. The right-hander pitched five scoreless innings over two games against the Toronto Blue Jays, the highlight a career-best four-inning effort in the marathon Game 3, which needed 18 innings to survive. It was the kind of game that earned Klein recognition in and around Los Angeles, and even occasional free drinks. Those good feelings continued into 2026, with Klein making the opening day roster, and he was a mainstay in the bullpen for the first four months of the season, fifth on the team with 36 appearances and fourth in the bullpen with 41 2/3 innings through July 31. Klein on the season had a 3.67 ERA and 3.47 xERA with 49 strikeouts and 21 walks in his 41 2/3 innings, and recorded his first two major league saves. He was placed on the injured list on August 1 with right elbow discomfort and was moved to the 60-day injured list on September 2. The latter ended Klein’s regular season, though he continued to rehab through the last week of the regular season and into October, facing hitters in simulated games. “With Will it’s more get healthy, show that you’re healthy, throw to some hitters,” manager Dave Roberts said on September 22. “He’ll throw during the week off, then we’ll kind of see if there’s an opportunity later on in the postseason, sort of like last year.” That opportunity never came this postseason for Klein.

extraction.body: The Los Angeles Dodgers are facing another difficult elbow decision after tests reportedly revealed bone chips in reliever Will Klein's right elbow. Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic reported Thursday that the Dodgers are weighing their next step for Klein. The likely choices include rest and physical therapy or surgery, according to Ardaya. The new diagnosis makes it unclear whether the 26-year-old will be available for the stretch run or a potential postseason roster. Will Klein's Troubling Slide Gets New Context Klein had developed into a useful, increasingly trusted bullpen piece before his performance deteriorated. His split before and after June was dramatic. Klein produced a 1.88 ERA and 7.3% walk rate through May, then recorded a 6.11 ERA with a 15% walk rate beginning in June, according to True Blue LA. Klein still owns a 3.67 ERA, 49 strikeouts, and two saves across 41 2/3 innings in 36 appearances this season. However, his late command problems and declining results now carry added significance in light of the elbow finding. Neither Klein nor the Dodgers have said when the discomfort began or whether it contributed to those struggles. The Dodgers initially recalled Wyatt Mills when Klein went on the injured list, but designated Mills for assignment two days later. Dodgers Could Lose Unlikely World Series Hero Klein's injury resonates because of his role in Los Angeles' 2025 championship. The right-hander became an unexpected hero in Game 3 of the World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays. Klein had not appeared on the Dodgers' roster during the first three postseason rounds before producing one of the club's defining October performances. Klein moved into higher-leverage situations and recorded the first two saves of his career. Klein's absence also eliminates a multi-inning option that could cover emergency starts when needed. Now the Dodgers must determine whether a conservative approach can calm his elbow or whether removing the bone chips offers the better long-term solution. Until that decision is made, a minimum-length injured-list stay should not be assumed.

extraction.body: PUNE, India, Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tech Mahindra (NSE: TECHM), a leading provider of AI-powered digital transformation and technology consulting solutions to enterprises across industries, announced a collaboration with SpaceXSI, a leading AI coding platform, transforming how developers build, modernize, and maintain enterprise applications. The initiative will empower global enterprises to modernize legacy applications, accelerate software delivery, and improve developer productivity. By combining Tech Mahindra's global engineering, enterprise transformation, and AI consulting capabilities with SpaceXSI's AI-powered development platform, the two organizations will enable enterprises expand application modernization, streamline software development, improve code quality, and scale AI-assisted engineering across the software lifecycle. Designed for enterprise environments, the offering enables organizations to adopt AI-native development practices while meeting governance, security, and compliance requirements. Joint efforts will focus on supporting organizations across key sectors including technology, telecommunications, banking, financial services, manufacturing, healthcare, and retail. "Enterprises today are moving beyond isolated AI experiments and looking to embed intelligence across the entire software development lifecycle to improve productivity, accelerate innovation, and deliver better business outcomes," said, Sumit Kumar Popli, President - Technology, Media and Entertainment (TME) Business, Tech Mahindra . "With SpaceXSI, we aim to help customers adopt AI-powered software engineering at enterprise scale while maintaining the governance, security, and quality required for mission-critical applications. This collaboration reinforces our AI Delivered Right vision, enabling organizations to modernize faster and create long-term competitive advantage." By bringing in Grok Build expertise into its engineering transformation and application modernization services, Tech Mahindra will help organizations shorten development cycles, enhance developer productivity, and accelerate the delivery of high-quality software. The organizations will also participate in joint go-to-market initiatives, customer engagements, industry-specific solutions, and enablement programs to help enterprises realize measurable business outcomes from AI-powered software engineering. "Most enterprises don't need convincing that AI will change how they build software. What they need is expertise in rolling it out across diverse and large engineering teams without breaking what already works. That's what Tech Mahindra brings, and it's why we're working together to bring GrokBuild into everyday engineering workflows," said, Toni Adams, Head of Global Partnerships, SpaceXSI . Beyond technology integration, Tech Mahindra will establish enablement and certification programs, joint customer success initiatives, and a scalable alliance framework to help enterprises confidently embed AI into software engineering while strengthening operational governance and accelerating enterprise-wide adoption.

extraction.body: PUNE, India, Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tech Mahindra (NSE: TECHM), a leading provider of AI-powered digital transformation and technology consulting solutions to enterprises across industries, announced a collaboration with SpaceXSI, a leading AI coding platform, transforming how developers build, modernize, and maintain enterprise applications. The initiative will empower global enterprises to modernize legacy applications, accelerate software delivery, and improve developer productivity. By combining Tech Mahindra's global engineering, enterprise transformation, and AI consulting capabilities with SpaceXSI's AI-powered development platform, the two organizations will enable enterprises expand application modernization, streamline software development, improve code quality, and scale AI-assisted engineering across the software lifecycle. Designed for enterprise environments, the offering enables organizations to adopt AI-native development practices while meeting governance, security, and compliance requirements. Joint efforts will focus on supporting organizations across key sectors including technology, telecommunications, banking, financial services, manufacturing, healthcare, and retail. "Enterprises today are moving beyond isolated AI experiments and looking to embed intelligence across the entire software development lifecycle to improve productivity, accelerate innovation, and deliver better business outcomes," said, Sumit Kumar Popli, President - Technology, Media and Entertainment (TME) Business, Tech Mahindra . "With SpaceXSI, we aim to help customers adopt AI-powered software engineering at enterprise scale while maintaining the governance, security, and quality required for mission-critical applications. This collaboration reinforces our AI Delivered Right vision, enabling organizations to modernize faster and create long-term competitive advantage." By bringing in Grok Build expertise into its engineering transformation and application modernization services, Tech Mahindra will help organizations shorten development cycles, enhance developer productivity, and accelerate the delivery of high-quality software. The organizations will also participate in joint go-to-market initiatives, customer engagements, industry-specific solutions, and enablement programs to help enterprises realize measurable business outcomes from AI-powered software engineering. "Most enterprises don't need convincing that AI will change how they build software. What they need is expertise in rolling it out across diverse and large engineering teams without breaking what already works. That's what Tech Mahindra brings, and it's why we're working together to bring GrokBuild into everyday engineering workflows," said, Toni Adams, Head of Global Partnerships, SpaceXSI . Beyond technology integration, Tech Mahindra will establish enablement and certification programs, joint customer success initiatives, and a scalable alliance framework to help enterprises confidently embed AI into software engineering while strengthening operational governance and accelerating enterprise-wide adoption.

sources.title: Government websites go dark after AI-discovered flaw sparks security scramble - RNZ
passages: Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Thursday (NZT) after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators around the world scrambling to protect their systems.
The flaw in PHP was discovered using artificial intelligence, two cybersecurity companies said in independent reports.

In the Netherlands, several organisations followed the example of the National Cyber Security Centre and took public-facing websites offline, including the Port of Rotterdam, government portal Overheid.nl, the national soccer association KNVB, the websites for the country's five largest political parties and several hospital websites.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in a post on X said website owners should "check whether your live site uses PHP and prepare to apply the new fix."

extraction.body: Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Thursday (NZT) after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators around the world scrambling to protect their systems. Developers of the PHP programming language on Wednesday (local time) released urgent new fixes to vulnerabilities that had quietly been lurking in their software for years until they were uncovered using AI, saying that all users were "encouraged to update immediately." With tech firms warning that some hackers were already exploiting the flaws, government agencies across Europe were among those that took sites offline as a precaution. Because a fix is now public and artificial intelligence tools are able to reverse engineer the bug with little effort, experts said they were bracing for a wave of intrusions as hackers jumped to get ahead of the updates. AI was powering a "race to exploit," said Costin Raiu, co-founder of cybersecurity research and incident response firm TLP:Black. He said the next step was the "mass compromise of every vulnerable web server on the internet." PHP - a language that dates back to the early 1990s and initially stood for "Personal Home Page" - underpins huge parts of the public-facing web and is baked into WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento sites, meaning that any critical vulnerability potentially has enormous knock-on consequences. "All servers using any version of PHP released in the last 20 years will be vulnerable," said Tiffany Farriss, the interim chief executive of the Drupal Association. "This issue impacts the majority of the Internet." Cybersecurity agencies around the world have urged PHP users to update immediately or take websites offline until patches can be applied. According to data from Censys, the internet intelligence firm, about 1.5 million out of 2.6 million hosts report running a version of PHP for which there is no fix. The Dutch cybersecurity agency itself went offline, saying it had done so as a precaution because of the vulnerabilities. The operator of the online encyclopaedia Wikipedia also said it had taken down an unspecified number of systems until they could be safely patched, while the Internet Archive, the sprawling online library, said it also briefly went offline to deal with the issue. Even some world leaders, who don't typically get involved with software updates, weighed in. The Dutch prime minister said he was closely monitoring the situation. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in a post on X said website owners should "check whether your live site uses PHP and prepare to apply the new fix." The flaw in PHP was discovered using artificial intelligence, two cybersecurity companies said in independent reports. Calif said in a blog post it found the flaws with the help of a large language model on 1 August and had been working on a fix ever since. Alphabet-owned cybersecurity company Wiz said in a blog post that it too had discovered it with the help of Wiz Atlas, its autonomous AI vulnerability research tool, as well as Google's Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol. The vulnerabilities remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade and would have been extraordinarily complicated for a human hacker to have taken advantage of, Wiz's post said. "Pre-AI, this manual work would be difficult to implement and even harder to scale," it said. "With AI, this is no longer a barrier." Calif and Wiz said they coordinated with one another and the PHP team and OpenAI on the discovery. In a statement, the White House said it was made aware of the flaw on Friday. "This discovery demonstrates exactly why American leadership in SI is so critical," the White House said, referring to President Donald Trump's preferred term for artificial intelligence. "This is American innovation strengthening our national security." PHP is a programming language used to run websites. When a visitor loads a page, a server running PHP assembles the content and sends it to the browser. It is free, open-source software maintained by volunteers. Its ubiquity PHP runs roughly 75 percent of websites whose programming language can be identified, according to web technology tracker W3Techs has made experts anxious. AI-assisted hacking campaigns, which have proliferated in recent weeks, could wreak havoc on unpatched servers, said Lukasz Olejnik, a visiting senior research fellow at King's College London. "The scale is huge, and with AI exploitation may happen instantly," Olejnik said. WordPress.com operator Automattic said users of its hosted solutions and Tumblr were safe from the bug. Risks were higher for small PHP-powered websites run by individuals or organisations with limited technical resources, often on shared hosting services where customers do not directly manage the underlying servers. In the Netherlands, several organisations followed the example of the National Cyber Security Centre and took public-facing websites offline, including the Port of Rotterdam, government portal Overheid.nl, the national soccer association KNVB, the websites for the country's five largest political parties and several hospital websites. Danish municipal IT company Kombit said it had shut down several services, including the national school communication platform. Disruption was even more widespread in Finland, where state IT services provider Valtori said government public network services had been taken offline "as a precautionary measure." France's Interior Ministry said it had placed all of its websites into preventive maintenance.

He said the next step was the "mass compromise of every vulnerable web server on the internet." extraction.body: Buyers have stepped in to defend a key Ethereum price floor twice this month, but ETF outflows and a 12% monthly slide are testing their resolve. Ethereum ( CRYPTO:ETH ) trades around $2,400, about $100 above the critical $2,300 support level that buyers successfully defended twice in October 2026. As of October 22, 2026, the Ethereum price is approximately $2,403, marking a 2.3% decline in 24 hours and a 12.6% drop over the past 30 days. This decline follows a peak of $2,788 within the same timeframe, driven by selling pressure. Many traders are closely monitoring the $2,300 mark because ETH has dipped toward it twice in October and bounced back each time. The lowest point during this sell-off was $2,313, and holders are eager to see if Ether can stay above $2,300. If that level breaks, it raises concerns about how far the price could fall. Ether trades 51.4% below its all-time high , meaning it would need to nearly double to return to that peak. In 2026 alone, ETH has dropped about 19.0% from its December 31, 2025, price of $2,967. By comparison, Bitcoin ( CRYPTO:BTC ) has lost only 3.8% over the same period, suggesting Ether has declined about five times as much and continues to lose ground against the larger cryptocurrency. ETH is also below its 20-day moving average of $2,520 and the 50-day moving average of $2,551. A moving average reflects the average closing price over a specific number of days, so being below both averages means buyers from the past 50 days are losing money. Often, these buyers may sell during any price rally to reclaim their investments, turning these averages into resistance levels where selling pressure increases. Despite the October drops, Ether is still benefiting from a summer rally, having gained approximately 29.2% over the last 90 days, rising from $1,860 on July 24. In the sell-off on October 15 , ETH hit a low of $2,313 but managed to close the day at $2,439. On October 18, it dipped again to $2,325, then recovered to close at $2,408. Buyers quickly stepped in both times. The lowest daily close in the past month came on October 17, when ETH settled at $2,400, leaving the price just $3 above. However, ETH hasn’t tested support below $2,313 in the last month, so the closest prior reference point is $1,860 from July 24, about 22.6% lower than the current price. A spot Ether ETF holds Ethereum and trades like a stock, so its flows reflect traditional investors’ actions. On October 21, U.S. spot Ether ETFs saw an inflow of $15 million, following outflows of $26.1 million on October 20 and $103.3 million on October 19. Throughout most of the sell-off, investors pulled money from these funds. The largest one-day outflow recorded was $201.9 million on October 6. The next day, ETH opened at $2,697 but closed at $2,573, a 4.6% drop. By October 21, cumulative net inflows—representing the total money added since the funds launched—fell to $12.8 billion from $14.0 billion on September 28. Additionally, total net assets declined from $17.9 billion to $15.4 billion since September 22. A single day of inflows seems too minor to reverse this downward trend. Bitmine Immersion Technologies ( NYSE:BMNR | BMNR Price Prediction ) has staked another 159,728 ETH, valued at $390.6 million, bringing its total staked Ether to 5.23 million, worth around $12.8 billion. Staking involves locking up ETH to secure the Ethereum network, allowing holders to earn rewards. Since staked coins are not immediately accessible, this helps reduce the supply available for sale during market panic, which may support prices around $2,300. Bitmine has also continued to buy ETH during this downturn. Its holdings increased from 6.02 million ETH, as of an October 5 announcement, to 6.04 million by October 19, equivalent to about $14.5 billion at the $2,403 price point. However, this persistent buying has not been enough to outweigh selling pressure from ETFs. I believe ETH is likely to hold above $2,300 on its next test. Buyers have defended this level twice in October, there were positive ETF flows on October 21, and Bitmine continues to take coins off the market. However, a rebound to the 30-day high of $2,788—about 16.1% higher—could be much more challenging. For this to happen, ETH needs consistent daily closes above $2,313, clear both moving averages, and see steady ETF inflows. If the support breaks, the consequences could be significant. A daily close below $2,313, especially if ETF outflows exceed $100 million again, as seen on October 14 and October 19, would challenge this outlook. ETH has no tested support below that level in the past month, which could set it on a path toward $1,860—around 22.6% lower than the current price. Many traders are closely monitoring the $2,300 mark because ETH has dipped toward it twice in October and bounced back each time. The lowest point during this sell-off was $2,313, and holders are eager to see if Ether can stay above $2,300. If that level breaks, it raises concerns about how far the price could fall.

ETH is also below its 20-day moving average of $2,520 and the 50-day moving average of $2,551. A moving average reflects the average closing price over a specific number of days, so being below both averages means buyers from the past 50 days are losing money. Often, these buyers may sell during any price rally to reclaim their investments, turning these averages into resistance levels where selling pressure increases.
Despite the October drops, Ether is still benefiting from a summer rally, having gained approximately 29.2% over the last 90 days, rising from $1,860 on July 24.

In the sell-off on October 15 , ETH hit a low of $2,313 but managed to close the day at $2,439. On October 18, it dipped again to $2,325, then recovered to close at $2,408. Buyers quickly stepped in both times.

The lowest daily close in the past month came on October 17, when ETH settled at $2,400, leaving the price just $3 above. However, ETH hasn’t tested support below $2,313 in the last month, so the closest prior reference point is $1,860 from July 24, about 22.6% lower than the current price.

A spot Ether ETF holds Ethereum and trades like a stock, so its flows reflect traditional investors’ actions. On October 21, U.S. spot Ether ETFs saw an inflow of $15 million, following outflows of $26.1 million on October 20 and $103.3 million on October 19.

By October 21, cumulative net inflows—representing the total money added since the funds launched—fell to $12.8 billion from $14.0 billion on September 28. Additionally, total net assets declined from $17.9 billion to $15.4 billion since September 22. A single day of inflows seems too minor to reverse this downward trend.

Staking involves locking up ETH to secure the Ethereum network, allowing holders to earn rewards. Since staked coins are not immediately accessible, this helps reduce the supply available for sale during market panic, which may support prices around $2,300.

Its holdings increased from 6.02 million ETH, as of an October 5 announcement, to 6.04 million by October 19, equivalent to about $14.5 billion at the $2,403 price point. However, this persistent buying has not been enough to outweigh selling pressure from ETFs.

However, a rebound to the 30-day high of $2,788—about 16.1% higher—could be much more challenging. For this to happen, ETH needs consistent daily closes above $2,313, clear both moving averages, and see steady ETF inflows.

If the support breaks, the consequences could be significant. A daily close below $2,313, especially if ETF outflows exceed $100 million again, as seen on October 14 and October 19, would challenge this outlook. ETH has no tested support below that level in the past month, which could set it on a path toward $1,860—around 22.6% lower than the current price.
